findings.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:52-56 — Any **attendee** of a booking gets the same write power as the organizer (`isAttendee` matched on `attendee.email === user.email`). Attendee rows are self-supplied at booking time, and it is transitive — a guest added by this mutation becomes an attendee and inherits the power. Combined with #2, an external booker can relay unlimited ICS invites from the org's domain with the organizer's Reply-To.

addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`, no `.min(1)`, no uniqueness refine, and no normalization. The only uniqueness check lives in the client dialog and is bypassed by calling the endpoint directly. Duplicates *within* one request are never filtered — the server dedupe at `handler.ts:74-78` only compares against *pre-existing* attendees. One request → N duplicate attendee rows + N emails.

addGuests.handler.ts:1` (whole change) — 555 lines of state-mutating behavior — DB writes, external calendar mutation, email fan-out — ship with **zero** test files of any kind. The permission matrix (owner/admin/member/organizer/attendee × personal/team) has no coverage; the AND/OR inversion in #4 is exactly what a table-driven permission test catches on first run.
addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `isTeamAdminOrOwner = isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` — AND where the variable name and intent say OR. A genuine team ADMIN who is not the owner gets `FORBIDDEN`.

addGuests.handler.ts:70-78 — Blacklist entries are `.toLowerCase()`'d but the incoming guest is compared verbatim (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses the block. Entries are also never `.trim()`'d after `split(",")`, so any whitespace after a comma makes that entry permanently dead. The one abuse control in the handler, defeated by a capital letter.

addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the **raw input array**, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`. `email-manager.ts:541` branches on that list to pick template, so any pre-existing attendee whose address is replayed receives a fresh full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` re-invite (with a REQUEST-method ICS) — on demand, repeatedly, with no DB change to audit. Blacklisted addresses re-enter the classification set too.

addGuests.handler.ts:158-165 — EventManager is built from the **caller's** credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, `...user`) while `evt.destinationCalendar` and `booking.uid` belong to the organizer. `booking.user.credentials` is fetched at :35-39 and never used. When an attendee or team admin calls this, the calendar update runs with credentials that have no grant on the organizer's calendar — it silently no-ops and the handler still returns success. Classic silent pass.

addGuests.handler.ts:22-44 — No `booking.status` or `endTime` check. CANCELLED, REJECTED, PENDING and long-past bookings are all accepted, and both templates hardcode `status: "CONFIRMED"` / `method: "REQUEST"`. Adding a guest to a cancelled booking re-broadcasts a CONFIRMED REQUEST for the same UID, resurrecting the event on **every existing attendee's** calendar. A calendar-spoofing primitive available to any attendee.

addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 vs 165 — Attendees are committed to the DB *before* the unguarded `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, with no transaction and no compensation. A provider failure throws after the write lands: DB says the guest is on the booking, the real calendar doesn't have them, and no email is ever sent because the throw precedes `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

addGuests.handler.ts:74-81 — **The retry path is permanently broken.** After the partial failure in #9, the attendees already exist, so a retry hits the `uniqueGuests.length === 0` guard and throws `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid`. The user is told it failed, then told they're duplicates, and can never get the invite sent. Only a DB-level fix unsticks it.

addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` — `err` discarded entirely, no logger, no bookingId, no stack, and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` with a green toast. Total SMTP outage is indistinguishable from success to both callers and operators. Nothing is queued or retried.

addGuests.handler.ts:74-106 — Read-then-write race: the dedupe reads `booking.attendees` from the earlier `findFirst`, then a separate `booking.update`/`createMany` inserts without re-checking. No transaction, no unique constraint. Two concurrent calls (double-click, retried request, two admins) both pass and both insert → duplicate attendees and duplicate invites. `handleAdd` has no in-flight guard beyond the button's `loading` prop.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 — Component inside `@calcom/ui` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` **from its own barrel** `@calcom/ui`, which re-exports this very module at `index.tsx:153`. Require cycle through a newly-public entry point; can yield `undefined` components / "Element type is invalid" depending on bundler eval order, and pulls the full ~150-export barrel into the chunk, defeating the `dynamic()` split whose stated rationale is "these are like 40kb". Sibling form components import by relative path for exactly this reason.

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-31 — A zod schema is declared **inside the component body** (recreated every render) and named `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` — colliding with the exported server schema of the same name but a different shape. The uniqueness `.refine` exists only here, so the real contract at `addGuests.schema.ts:5` accepts duplicates. Two contradictory definitions under one name across the client/server boundary.

organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26 — `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` is unguarded while every other field in the file uses optional chaining. Throws TypeError on an empty attendee list; and since new guests are created with `name: ""` (`handler.ts:85`), if a new guest sorts first the subject reads `Guests Added: X with  at …`. The attendee template uses a `team?.name

addGuests.handler.ts:126-160 — `evt` never sets `team` (nor `iCalUID`, `bookerUrl`, `additionalNotes`, `responses`). `sendAddGuestsEmails` gates team-host notification on `calendarEvent.team?.members` (`email-manager.ts:531`), so that entire branch is **dead** — for team bookings no host other than `booking.user` is ever notified. Team bookings are the case this feature handles worst.

addGuests.handler.ts:92-102, 136-146 — Guests are written straight into `booking.attendees` with no `BookingSeat` record and no seats handling, despite the handler reading `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees`. Seat capacity is never checked, the full attendee roster is disclosed in outgoing ICS contrary to `seatsShowAttendees`, and the created attendees have no working cancel/reschedule link.

addGuests.handler.ts:88-102, 173 — No `BOOKING_UPDATED` webhook or workflow trigger is emitted, unlike every other booking-mutating route. Downstream integrations and automations never learn the attendee set changed and permanently diverge from Cal's state.

addGuests.handler.ts:47-48 — `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` launders a nullable id into a real-looking team id, issuing two pointless membership lookups for team `0` on every personal booking. It fails closed only because no team row has id 0 — there is no explicit guard, so any change to those helpers' falsy-id handling turns this into a full IDOR on every personal booking.
addGuests.handler.ts:58-66 — `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId \

email-manager.ts:525-548 — `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)` is fail-fast: one rejected send (bad address, SMTP 550) rejects the aggregate, discards the other rejections, and leaves the caller unable to tell who actually received mail. Combined with #11, partial delivery reports as full success, and re-driving would double-send. `Promise.allSettled` with per-recipient logging is the right shape.

addGuests.handler.ts:165 — No timeout, deadline, or cancellation on `updateCalendarAttendees`, which does outbound HTTP to third-party APIs inside a synchronous tRPC mutation. A provider brownout holds requests and their DB connections open — a connection-pool exhaustion vector for the whole web tier. Email fan-out is likewise inline rather than dispatched to the background tasker used elsewhere for post-booking side effects.

addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `updateCalendarAttendees`' return value is discarded — no per-destination success inspection, no `booking.references` update, no broken-integration fallback. If EventManager reports results in a `results[]` array (the pattern its `create`/`update` methods use) rather than throwing, a failure against one of several connected calendars is completely invisible. *(EventManager absent from checkout.)*

addGuests.handler.ts:80-81, 173 — Silent partial success: submit 5 guests, have 4 filtered as blacklisted/existing, and the response is the same flat `{ message: "Guests added" }` with a green toast. Only the all-zero case errors — and it errors with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which misdescribes the condition (the input *was* valid and unique; it was a no-op, or a blacklist hit). Callers can't distinguish malformed input from already-attending from blocked, so they can't retry or message correctly.

addGuests.handler.ts:167-173 — No rate limiting (`checkRateLimitAndThrowError` is used on comparable cal.com mutations) and no audit trail — the only record that guests were added is the console line on failure. An abuser can loop the endpoint indefinitely with nothing throttling or alerting, and post-incident there is no log of who added whom to which booking.

attendee-add-guests-email.ts:11-19`, `organizer-add-guests-email.ts:12-20 — The ICS is regenerated with `method: "REQUEST"` for the same `evt.uid`, but the handler never bumps `iCalSequence` and never sets `iCalUID`. Per RFC 5546 a REQUEST with an unchanged SEQUENCE is a duplicate — Outlook/Google may drop the update entirely, or re-prompt every existing attendee to RSVP to a meeting they already accepted. Either way "the calendar invite was updated" can silently be false.

email-manager.ts:525-537 — `sendAddGuestsEmails` omits the `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` checks that the immediately-preceding `sendLocationChangeEmails` applies, and the handler never loads or passes `eventTypeMetadata`. Event types configured to suppress emails still emit on this path, violating an explicit customer setting with no way to turn it off.

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — `t(err.message)` treats every TRPCError message as an i18n key, but zod parse failures surface `err.message` as a JSON-stringified array of issues. The user is shown a raw zod JSON blob prefixed with `BAD_REQUEST:`. The route's implicit "message is always a translation key" contract is violated by the schema layer with nothing enforcing it.

addGuests.handler.ts:124-152 — The ~30-line booking→`CalendarEvent` mapping (plus the `videoCallReference` block and the `attendeesListPromises`/`getTranslation` fan-out at :106-121) is a verbatim third copy of the same construction in `editLocation.handler.ts`/`requestReschedule.handler.ts`. Every new CalendarEvent field must be replayed by hand in N places and rots in the ones missed — this is how #16's missing `team` happens. Should be a shared `buildCalendarEventFromBooking()`. *(Siblings absent from checkout; inferred from identical idioms.)*

organizer-add-guests-email.ts:1-38`, `attendee-add-guests-email.ts:1-34 — The two new payload classes are the existing `*-location-change-email` builders with three i18n keys swapped; the icalEvent block, from/to/replyTo assembly and `getTextBody` call are identical between the two new files as well. The cheap abstraction is demonstrated one directory over — the React wrappers are 8-line prop-overrides. Re-copying the whole payload is how ICS `method`/`status` drift out of sync across the ~10 sibling templates.

packages/ui/index.tsx:153`, `MultiEmail.tsx:5-14 — New public `@calcom/ui` export with no versioning story and a wrong signature: `value` is typed required but defensively defaulted at :14 by **reassigning the prop** (`value = value

MultiEmail.tsx:11-95 — New barrel-exported shared component with zero test coverage: add/remove-by-index, the two render branches, `readOnly` hiding both buttons. Rows are `key={index}`, so removing an index while another input is focused re-keys the list — the classic stale-value bug, and the single behavior most worth a test here.

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:78`, `MultiEmail.tsx:57, 83 — Three `data-testid`s (`add_members`, `add-another-email`, `add-emails`) added with no consuming spec anywhere. `add_members` is also applied to the dialog's submit button while `BookingListItem.tsx:193` uses the same string as the menu item's `id` — any future selector will be ambiguous. Testids without specs give a false impression of e2e coverage.

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:98 — `addGuestsMutation.isPending` is the tRPC v11 / react-query v5 flag; tRPC v10 (which this router's `UNSTABLE_HANDLER_CACHE` pattern is characteristic of) exposes `isLoading`. If the repo is on v10 the button never enters its loading state and users can double-submit — which, with #2 and #12, produces duplicate attendee rows. `package.json` is absent from the checkout; worth one grep of the lockfile.

addGuests.handler.ts:52, 76`; `email-manager.ts:541 — Email identity is compared case-sensitively in three places that must agree: the authz predicate, the dedupe filter, and the template-selection branch. The same human in different casing is simultaneously "not an attendee", "not a duplicate", and routed to the wrong email template. The authz predicate and the data it guards disagree about identity.

MultiEmail.tsx:46 — `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is a hardcoded English string in a component that already has `const { t } = useLocale()` and calls `t("add_another")` twelve lines below. Ships untranslated to every locale, and being in the shared ui package it surfaces in every future consumer.
AddGuestsDialog.tsx:40-42 — `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` is a template literal, always truthy — so `\

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33, 76, 90 — `isInvalidEmail` is a one-way latch — set on failed parse, cleared only by the Cancel button. Not cleared on input change, on successful validation, on mutation success, or on ESC/backdrop dismiss (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` at :58 bypasses all reset logic, so `multiEmailValue` also survives and reopening shows previously typed guests).
AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51 — `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) return;` bails silently after the user removes every row — clicking "Add" does nothing, no toast, no inline message. Dead-end state.

addGuests.handler.ts:173 — `return { message: "Guests added" }` — a hardcoded English literal, while every *error* path in the same handler returns an i18n **key**. Two conventions mixed within one handler, and the field is dead on arrival: the UI ignores it and renders `t("guests_added")`. Return the key, or return the updated attendee list.

BookingListItem.tsx:193-200 — The "add guests" action is appended unconditionally, with no gating on status (cancelled/rejected/pending) or past bookings — unlike the surrounding status-scoped actions in this file. The client is the only place #8 could have been caught pre-server, and it doesn't try.

MultiEmail.tsx:13-14, 73-88 — `value.length ? (...) : <></>` at :17/:74 is immediately followed by a mutually exclusive `{!value.length && !readOnly && ...}` at :77 — the same predicate tested twice with a dead `<></>` branch between. The two "add an email" buttons at :55 and :78 duplicate identical `[...value].push("")` handlers that must be kept in sync by hand.

src/templates/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx:3-9`, `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail.tsx:4-10 — `{...props}` is spread **after** `title`/`subject`/`headerType`, so a caller passing those keys silently overrides the template's identity. These are now public exports from the templates barrel; spread first if overrides are unintended, last if they are. Currently reads as accidental.

attendee-add-guests-email.ts:29`, `src/templates/index.ts:38-39 — `renderEmail("AttendeeAddGuestsEmail", ...)` resolves the template by **string key** against the barrel. Nothing tests that these two keys resolve; a rename or missed export fails only at send time — inside the swallowed catch of #11. A one-line "every renderEmail key resolves" test converts a silent production email outage into a build failure.

_router.tsx:79-94 — The new procedure copies the 16-line `UNSTABLE_HANDLER_CACHE` lazy-import block verbatim, including the `// Unreachable code but required for type safety` comment and the redundant second null check. Consistent with the file, so not wrong here — but this is the 12th copy, and the marginal cost that makes a `lazyHandler(...)` helper worth extracting.

This is a real permission/authorization issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out already-existing attendee emails and blacklisted emails, and only `uniqueGuests` are persisted via `createMany`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input `guests` array. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), the per-attendee template selection uses `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide who is treated as a “new guest” and gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a full re-invite with ICS REQUEST). Passing the unfiltered list means an already-existing attendee email re-submitted in the UI will be classified as “new” and receive a fresh scheduled/re-invite email even though no DB change occurred for that attendee. Similarly, if an existing attendee email is in the blacklist, it was excluded from `uniqueGuests` but would still be in `guests` and thus affect classification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:158-165 — EventManager is built from the **caller's** credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, `...user`) while `evt.destinationCalendar` and `booking.uid` belong to the organizer. `booking.user.credentials` is fetched at :35-39 and never used. When an attendee or team admin calls this, the calendar update runs with credentials that have no grant on the organizer's calendar — it silently no-ops and the handler still returns success. Classic silent pass.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `addGuestsHandler` can be invoked by non-organizers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner). Yet the calendar update is performed with the *caller’s* identity/credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`. At the same time, the booking data being updated/targeted (`booking.uid`, `evt.destinationCalendar` derived from `booking.destinationCalendar` / `booking.user.destinationCalendar`) is tied to the organizer/booking owner, and `booking.user.credentials` is explicitly fetched in the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { user: { include: { credentials: true }}})` but never used. This is a concrete, verifiable mismatch in the diff and is likely to prevent updating the organizer’s external calendar when an attendee/admin triggers the mutation (and the handler still proceeds to return success if `updateCalendarAttendees` no-ops rather than throwing).

After mutating attendees, it calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The newly added email templates (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) generate an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` and use the booking UID, so invoking this for a cancelled/ended booking can emit a CONFIRMED REQUEST update for the same event to existing attendees, which can cause calendar clients to re-add/re-confirm the event. This is a concrete, diff-visible correctness/security risk enabled by the lack of status/time checks plus attendee-level access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 vs 165 — Attendees are committed to the DB *before* the unguarded `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, with no transaction and no compensation. That calendar update is not wrapped in try/catch and there is no DB transaction or rollback/compensation. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., provider/API failure), the mutation will error after the DB write has already committed, leaving the booking’s attendees in the DB but not reflected in the external calendar. If there is no DB-level unique constraint on (bookingId,email), this can create duplicate attendee rows; if there is a constraint, it can still produce avoidable constraint errors. In the caller (`addGuests.handler.ts`), this throw is caught and only a generic log is emitted, so you lose per-recipient success/failure information and can end up with partial delivery while the system proceeds as if the operation succeeded. adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `message` is built via a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. Template literals always produce a string, and here it will at minimum include `": "` (and often `"undefined"` when `err.data?.code` is missing), so `message` will be truthy. Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` logic effectively dead and potentially displaying confusing output like `undefined: ...`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33, 76, 90 — `isInvalidEmail` is a one-way latch — set on failed parse, cleared only by the Cancel button. Not cleared on input change, on successful validation, on mutation success, or on ESC/backdrop dismiss (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` at :58 bypasses all reset logic, so `multiEmailValue` also survives and reopening shows previously typed guests).

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared on successful validation (before/after `mutate`) nor in `onSuccess` (which resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but does not call `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Additionally, the Dialog is controlled via `open={isOpenDialog}` and `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, so closing via ESC/backdrop will not run the Cancel reset logic; since the component remains mounted, both `isInvalidEmail` and `multiEmailValue` can persist across closes and reopens, causing the error banner and/or old inputs to reappear.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51 — `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) return;` bails silently after the user removes every row — clicking "Add" does nothing, no toast, no inline message. Dead-end state.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.handleAdd`, the code explicitly returns early when `multiEmailValue.length === 0` with no toast or inline validation. This state is reachable because `MultiEmail` lets the user remove rows via `onClickAddon`, and removing the last row sets the value to `[]`. In that situation, clicking the dialog’s “Add” button does nothing and provides no feedback, matching the finding (even though the UI also shows an “Add Emails” button when empty).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:173 — `return { message: "Guests added" }` — a hardcoded English literal, while every *error* path in the same handler returns an i18n **key**. Two conventions mixed within one handler, and the field is dead on arrival: the UI ignores it and renders `t("guests_added")`. Return the key, or return the updated attendee list.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the success path returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, a hardcoded English string. In the same handler, all TRPCError `message` values are i18n keys (e.g., `"booking_not_found"`, `"emails_must_be_unique_valid"`). In the added UI (`AddGuestsDialog`), the mutation `onSuccess` ignores the returned payload entirely and always shows `t("guests_added")`, so the returned message is currently unused. This makes the API response inconsistent and non-localizable for any consumer that *does* use `message`.

However, the finding’s core claim—that this is a defect because it should be gated by booking status/past time “unlike surrounding status-scoped actions”—is not verifiable from the diff provided (we can’t see the rest of `BookingListItem.tsx` to confirm how other actions are gated or whether `actions` is later filtered).
